# Judges Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_283.jpg, JDG_page_284.jpg

### Samson's Riddle

1. One day when Samson was in Timnah, one of the Philistine women caught his eye.

2. When he returned home, he told his father and mother, "A young Philistine woman in Timnah caught my eye. Get her for me as my wife."

3. His father and mother objected. "Isn't there even one woman in our tribe or among all the Israelites you could marry?" they asked. "Why must you go to the pagan Philistines to find a wife?" But Samson told his father, "Get her for me! She looks good to me."

4. His father and mother didn't realize the LORD was at work in this, creating an opportunity to act against the Philistines, who ruled over Israel at that time.

5. As Samson and his parents were going down to Timnah, a young lion suddenly came roaring at him near the vineyards of Timnah.

6. At that moment the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him, and he ripped the lion's jaws apart with his bare hands. He did it as easily as tearing apart a young goat. But he didn't tell his father or mother about it.

7. When he arrived in Timnah, he talked with the woman and liked her very much.

8. Later, when he returned to marry her, he turned off the path to look at the carcass of the lion. And he found that a swarm of bees had made honey in the carcass.

9. He scooped some of the honey into his hands and ate it along the way. He also gave some to his father and mother, and they ate it. But he didn't tell them he had taken the honey from the carcass of the lion.

10. His father went down to make arrangements for the wedding, and Samson prepared a feast there, as was the custom for young men.

11. When the bride's family saw him, they chose thirty young men to be his companions.

12. Samson said to them, "Let me tell you a riddle. If you solve it during these seven days of the celebration, I will give you thirty fine linen robes and thirty sets of clothes.

13. But if you can't solve it, then you must give me thirty fine linen robes and thirty sets of clothes." "All right," they agreed. "Tell us your riddle."

14. So he said: "Out of the eater came something to eat; out of the strong came something sweet." Three days later they were still trying to figure it out.

15. On the fourth day they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband into telling you the answer to the riddle, or we will burn down your father's house with you in it. Did you invite us to this party just to make us poor?"

16. So Samson's wife came to him in tears and said, "You don't really love me at all! You've given my friends a riddle, but you haven't told me the answer." "I haven't even told my father or mother," he replied. "Why should I tell you?"

17. She cried whenever she was with him throughout the entire celebration. At last, on the seventh day he told her the answer because she kept nagging him. Then she explained the riddle to the young men.

18. Before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the town came to Samson with the answer: "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" Samson replied, "If you hadn't plowed with my heifer, you wouldn't have solved my riddle!"

19. Then the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him. He went down to Ashkelon, killed thirty men, took their belongings, and gave their clothing to the men who had solved the riddle. But Samson was furious about what had happened, and he went back home to live with his father and mother.

20. So his wife was given in marriage to the man who had been Samson's best man at the wedding.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**"It was from the LORD" (v.4):** This is one of the most disturbing theological statements in Judges. Samson's lust for a Philistine woman — which violates everything a Nazirite should be — is "from the LORD." God doesn't cause Samson to sin, but God uses Samson's weakness as the trigger for conflict with the Philistines. This is the mystery of divine providence in Judges: God works through broken people, not perfect ones.

**The riddle (v.14):** "Out of the eater came something to eat; out of the strong came something sweet." The riddle is unfair — it's based on a private experience (the lion and the honey) that no one else could know. It was designed to be unsolvable. Samson wants to win; he's not interested in a fair game.

— PNEUMA, AI Translator
